api_library: Project Zomboid vanilla Lua/exposed engine APIs
symbol: isSittingOnFurniture / getSitOnFurnitureObject / getTilePositionCount / canReachTo (resting PC access)
returns: Observed furniture-sitting boolean and occupied IsoObject; observed positive seating-position count identifies furniture with sitting data. Native canReachTo returns same-floor neighboring reach with wall/door/window/stair checks. Native dispatch/conversion and effective seating replication NOT TESTED.
mutation: Framework reads native seating only. Vanilla rest/state processing owns furniture reference, flag, pose and recovery. Server revalidates authenticated actor; no framework seat persistence or custom replication.

evidence.statement: Rest wait records the actual furniture object on the character.
Native animated rest completes its timed action while allowing passive recovery and another activity; framework must not require a persistent rest action.
Server rest records occupied furniture; completion resets rest/bed, not furniture sitting. Shared furnitureHasSittingData calls SeatingManager getTilePositionCount.
Vanilla reads isSittingOnFurniture and getSitOnFurnitureObject together for a seated actor.
Stock Computer tiles appliances_com_01_72/73/74/75 declare Facing S/E/N/W.

Read-only inspection: IsoGameCharacter seating getters return native flag/object. PlayerSitOnFurnitureState enter/processOnEnter set sitting; exit clears it; enter uses SeatingManager adjacent position for actor placement. StatePacket server processing consumes the native state. IsoGridSquare.canReachTo bounds neighbors/same floor and tests door/window/wall/stair barriers. This describes native methods, not executed replication proof.

notes: Observed Lua call forms and bounded native inspection only. getTilePositionCount is used in shared RestAction including direction setup on server; furniture-sitting calls also appear in vanilla server building cursors. The framework uses the native actual furniture, never client flags. Unknown/custom PC Facing cannot extend reach. No SP/dedicated invocation or continuous endurance claim is proven; multi-tile seat choice and animation offsets remain runtime gates.
